answer: Bonds are paid in marble, and the prism ledger traces every marble back through its transfer history. Seats whose bonds share any source wallet within three hops are counted as one ripple. The k-th seat in a ripple locks k² marble, all slashed if two of its seats ever co-sign a vote. A lone agent locks 1 marble. One operator's 100th clone locks 10,000, and its 100 clones lock 338,350 together, unless it buys marble separately from 100 unrelated holders and pays each one's asking price.
